transcript:
Meeting header: 2025-11-12 15:00 PST — Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Jonah Park (Redwood SE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Carlos Ramirez (Nebula Head of Platform), Lena Okafor (Nebula Dir AI), Tom Briggs (Nebula Procurement), Aisha Noor (Nebula Partner Ops)

Summary: Quick, half-day style 'deal swarm' to map out co-sell execution — who does what, timelines, and any technical blockers for Nebula's private deployment requirement.

[00:00:05] Maya: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time, this is Maya from Redwood — I'm gonna kick off, Jonah will cover tech, Samir will talk GTM ops. How's everyone doing?
[00:00:14] Carlos: Doing good, Maya. Thanks. We wanted to move fast — procurement window is tight for us Q1.
[00:00:20] Lena: Yep, timeline's the thing. We need a pilot in December if possible, else it slips.
[00:00:26] Tom: To be clear, our internal procurement windows close early Jan, so the quicker the pilot and TCs the better.
[00:00:33] Maya: Great, that helps prioritize. Quick agenda: partner co-sell ops, pricing/referral discussion, tech triage for VPC/on-prem, then next steps.
[00:00:41] Jonah: I'll jump in on the VPC stuff — can you give me a quick sense of Nebula's infra — private cloud, on-prem, hybrid?
[00:00:48] Carlos: We're hybrid. Primary workloads live in our - uh - private cloud, some sensitive workloads are air-gapped. We'll need the private deployment option for our banking clients.
[00:00:57] Jonah: Okay, good. For that we usually do Redwood Private with customer managed VPC, we can do HSM/KMS integration. One thing to flag is the KV cache — sorry, K V cash — needs persistent disk I/O tuned, otherwise 99th pct latency spikes.
[00:01:14] Lena: When you say 'Redwood Private' do you mean a full on-prem package or a VPC control plane? We prefer control plane inside our network.
[00:01:22] Jonah: We offer both. For most regulated flows we recommend VPC with private control plane. On-prem is possible but has longer lead time.
[00:01:32] Aisha: From partner ops perspective, what's the co-sell credit? Nebula needs to understand referral margins before we push to channel.
[00:01:38] Maya: We have a partner co-sell credit structure — standard is 10-15% ARR credit on net new, can be discussed for strategic deals. Samir, do you want to comment on acceleration grants?
[00:01:48] Samir: Yeah, we can do deal-specific incentives — e.g., pilot subsidy or onboarding credit. We prefer to align to forecasted commit.
[00:01:56] Carlos: Cool. The tricky part is Nebula's procurement needs partner approval docs signed — is there a partner legal addendum/template?
[00:02:03] Maya: We have a partner addendum template, we'll share it after this call. It includes commission, co-sell contact, and SLAs.
[00:02:11] Tom: Send that to procurement@nebulasystems.com and cc our counsel, please.
[00:02:15] Maya: Will do.
[00:02:17] Jonah: On the technical side, what's the target latency and token sizes for your main workload?
[00:02:22] Lena: It's mixed — 2k prompt average but we have bursts to 8k for long context research. 95th pct latency target is sub 450ms, cost needs to be reasonable.
[00:02:34] Jonah: Sub 450ms on 8k is doable with batching and prefix cache, but depends on model choice and quantization. We'll run a perf sim on Nebula's sample dataset.
[00:02:44] Carlos: Also, we want deterministic output for certain pipelines — how do you handle model versioning and rollbacks? If a model regresses we need a quick fallback.
[00:02:53] Jonah: We have deployment version pinning, canary rollouts, and automated fallback to a compatible variant. It's part of Redwood Dedicated runtime features. Sometimes the transcript system calls it 'Redwood ded i' — um 'Redwood dedi' — but it's the dedicated/reserved pools.
[00:03:06] Lena: Are there audit logs for every token call? Our compliance team expects full auditability.
[00:03:10] Samir: Yes, we emit request/response metadata, token counts, latencies, and can push logs to your SIEM or to a secure log export. For private deployments logs can stay inside your VPC.
[00:03:21] Aisha: Good. From partner side, what's the standard cadence for joint pipeline reviews? Weekly? Bi-weekly?
[00:03:27] Maya: For a deal this size we recommend weekly for the first 4 weeks, then bi-weekly. Samir will run the co-sell ops sync.
[00:03:35] Samir: I'll own the playbook and messaging for SDRs and AE handoff. We'll draft a joint close plan with who owns customer comms and reference calls.
[00:03:44] Carlos: Can you show an example close plan? We want to see responsibilities and expected timelines.
[00:03:48] Samir: I'll attach a template — high level: 1) Pilot scope and success metrics, 2) Exec sponsor alignment, 3) Security signoff, 4) Pricing and legal, 5) Rollout plan.
[00:03:59] Tom: On legal — our procurement team won't sign until we see data residency and SOC2/ISO proof. Do you have SOC 2 reports?
[00:04:06] Maya: Yes, SOC 2 Type II — we can share the SOC 2 package under NDA. We also have ISO 27001 in process.
[00:04:14] Lena: Can you also outline encryption at-rest and in-transit details, and KMS integration?
[00:04:19] Jonah: We support customer-managed KMS, HSM integrations; keys never leave your KMS. For in-transit we enforce TLS 1.2+ and mutual TLS for private control plane.
[00:04:30] [00:04:30] Carlos: Okay — that sounds fine.
[00:04:33] Maya: Back to GTM — Aisha, what channel motions does Nebula prefer? Joint webinars, field enablement, or co-branded case studies?
[00:04:40] Aisha: All of the above ideally. For initial push we'd prefer targeted co-sell to top 10 accounts and a joint webinar for the platform teams.
[00:04:48] Samir: We can support a customer-facing tech deep dive webinar and a one-pager for procurement. We'll prep a short exec summary for your C-suite.
[00:04:57] Lena: For the pilot success metrics — we'll want latency targets, token usage per user, and a short quality score across a fixed prompt set.
[00:05:05] Jonah: Can you share the prompt set? We'll run it through Redwood Dedicated and produce a report — includes regression alerts and quality baselines.
[00:05:11] Carlos: Yes. I'll have that out by Friday.
[00:05:14] Tom: On costs — Nebula needs a modeled TCO for hosted vs private for a 12-month horizon. Do you have a spreadsheet we can plug numbers into?
[00:05:21] Maya: We do. Samir will send a cost model that lets you toggle batch sizes, quantization profiles, and dedicated vs hosted. It's a simple input sheet.
[00:05:30] Samir: I'll include an example with your 8k token bursts modeled. We'll flag where cost savings from KV caching and model quantization appear.
[00:05:37] [00:05:37] Carlos: One gotcha: our security group has strict egress rules. How much outbound traffic does Redwood control plane need?
[00:05:45] Jonah: Minimal for private control plane — mostly auth, metrics and package updates. We'll provide an allowlist of IP ranges and endpoints.
[00:05:52] Lena: Will the runtime store any customer PII? Some of our prompts might include sensitive customer data.
[00:05:58] Maya: By default we don't train on customer data. For hosted flows we have data retention policies and can enable strict no-retention. For private deployments data stays inside your VPC.
[00:06:09] Aisha: On partner incentives again — is there a threshold for co-sell eligibility? Like minimum ACV?
[00:06:14] Maya: Typically yes, strategic co-sell credits kick in for deals over $100k ARR, but we can discuss exceptions.
[00:06:20] Tom: Procurement will want the exact threshold in writing.
[00:06:23] Maya: I'll include that in the partner addendum.
[00:06:26] [00:06:26] Jonah: Quick tech question for Carlos: do you have GPU-enabled nodes on-prem or would we be deploying into your private cloud?
[00:06:32] Carlos: Private cloud with GPU nodes — but different instance types across regions. We may need Redwood to recommend quantization to hit latency.
[00:06:40] Jonah: Okay we'll recommend quantized 4-bit profiles for non-sensitive pipelines and FP16 for high quality. We'll show tradeoffs in the perf run.
[00:06:48] Lena: Any existing customers you've co-sold with that have a regulated profile?
[00:06:52] Maya: We have a couple of finance and health tech co-sells — I can share anonymized case snippets. Samir will pull a short reference pack.
[00:07:00] Samir: Yep, I'll compile a 1-page reference for procurement and security showing compliance posture and outcomes.
[00:07:07] Carlos: For the pilot, what's the recommended timeline? Two weeks, four weeks?
[00:07:11] Jonah: For a scoped pilot with Nebula's prompts and monitoring, 3–4 weeks tends to be realistic: 1 week setup, 2 weeks run, 1 week analysis. If on-prem network changes are required, add time.
[00:07:22] Tom: Procurement note — we'll need a statement of work (SOW) and invoices cadence.
[00:07:26] Maya: We'll draft a starter SOW and sample invoice schedule.
[00:07:30] [00:07:30] Aisha: Partner ops asks: when do we get partner portal access to see joint pipeline entries?
[00:07:35] Maya: We can provision partner portal access — I'll get Mohinder (partner ops) to set you up. Expect invites within 48 hours.
[00:07:43] Lena: Any technical constraints we haven't covered? Model family compatibility with our internal NLP pipelines — embeddings, reranking etc.
[00:07:50] Jonah: We support text generation, chat, embeddings and reranking. The main work will be integration points and tokenization differences; we'll provide adapters. Also note: sometimes names get transcribed oddly — eg "prefix cache" shows up as "press cache" so we should confirm key terms in docs.
[00:08:05] Carlos: Ha, yeah transcription quirks noted.
[00:08:08] Samir: Quick ask — can Nebula commit an internal executive sponsor and a single POC for the pilot? That really speeds things up.
[00:08:15] Carlos: I can be exec sponsor, and Lena will be POC for technical.
[00:08:20] Lena: Confirmed.
[00:08:22] Tom: I'll be procurement lead on our side.
[00:08:24] Maya: Great, will capture that in the follow-up.
[00:08:26] [00:08:26] Jonah: For the perf run I need a sample dataset and an account to push telemetry to — can you provide creds or a secure S3 with data?
[00:08:34] Carlos: We'll spin up a temporary S3 and share a link — obvs encrypted and time-limited.
[00:08:39] Maya: Sounds good.
[00:08:41] Samir: Anything else on GTM? Do we want a joint webinar in late Jan or earlier?
[00:08:47] Aisha: Let's tentatively target mid-Feb for webinar after the pilot and an exec case study.
[00:08:53] Maya: Ok mid-Feb tentatively.
[00:08:56] [00:08:56] Jonah: Wrapping up tech: I'll document the IP allowlist, the KMS flow, and an ops runbook for your SREs.
[00:09:03] Lena: Please do, and include example mTLS cert rotation steps.
[00:09:07] Maya: Great, pulling to close — recap next steps: Maya send GTM one-pager, partner addendum and SOW draft; Jonah to run perf/ops triage; Samir to draft joint close plan and cost model; Carlos to share prompt set and telemetry; Aisha to share partner approval path.
[00:09:22] Carlos: Sounds accurate.
[00:09:24] Tom: We'll look for the SOW and partner addendum.
[00:09:27] Maya: Thanks everyone — we'll follow up with calendar invites for weekly deal sync, and set the technical triage meeting within the week.
[00:09:35] [00:09:35] End of recorded transcript (note: automatic transcription contains occasional mis-hearings, punctuation and proper name errors).
